question: Should the corrected tail semantics intentionally invalidate all Codex, Claude, Vertex AI, and Pi cost-cache artifacts during upgrade?
rationale: The broad version bumps prevent stale offsets from skipping retained tails, but they also impose a one-time full rescan on every affected existing installation; accepting that compatibility cost requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Accept the full rebuild
options.body: Keep all four artifact bumps and merge after live proof demonstrates correct recovery and acceptable rebuild behavior.

options.title: Narrow the invalidation
options.body: Limit version bumps to artifact families proven to persist offsets affected by this scanner, with focused compatibility tests for unchanged providers.

options.title: Pause for migration design
options.body: Hold the PR until a more selective offset migration or repair strategy avoids discarding complete predecessor caches.

recommendation.title: Accept the full rebuild
recommendation.body: Keep all four artifact bumps and merge after live proof demonstrates correct recovery and acceptable rebuild behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the final scanner corrections and tests and are therefore best positioned to judge whether the broad cache invalidation is an acceptable upgrade tradeoff.
